docs.description:
Series identifier — swatch + label pairs naming each data series in a chart.

Variants:
  direction = horizontal (row, gap 16) | vertical (column, gap 8)
  items = 2 | 3 | 4 (number of series)

Each item: 10×10 swatch (radius/control, bound to data/category token) + label (label/sm bound to text/primary).

Defaults use category-06 / 02 / 04 / 07 (blue/orange/green/purple — colorblind-friendly mix). Override per instance via swatch fill swap.

rules.reason: A chart's legend, as the description says: each series' swatch beside its name, in a row (horizontal) or a column (vertical). The swatch is Figma's dot, the xs StatusIndicator's shape and edge, in the series' colour the caller gives (owner decision 2026-09-26), not a status. A list, one item per series.
A horizontal legend lays its items out in a row, a vertical one in a column, as its axis says.
A row's items are stack.md apart, a column's stack.xs, as Figma draws each.
A legend is as tall as its items: Figma has it fill its frame, which under a chart, in a column, is no height at all.
The dot is a SOLAR StatusIndicator (xs), whose 8px box is its own: the legend places it, and never sizes it.

The number of items is the caller's series, not a prop: Figma's 2, 3 and 4 are samples of it, drawn with the same item. The recipe keeps 4, the fullest; the oracle checks each count, reached by as many series.
A series' name is the caller's; Figma records no text prop, and names the text after its sample ("Active users").
The item's StatusIndicator is its series' swatch: Figma's dot, in the series' colour.
Figma's items are copies of one: a dot and a series' name. The shell draws one per series the caller gives, so the first stands for them all, checked as Figma draws it.
